text: You're scrolling for deals. And there it is: that one thing you need, at an unbelievably low price. A perfect score!
You rush to the store, excited. But when you arrive, the shelf is empty. 'Sold out,' a small sign confirms.
Again? Is it just bad luck, or do others always get there first? You wonder if it’s a glitch, or just poor planning.
But it's not bad luck. That cheap item, the 'loss leader,' was just bait. Its job was to get you inside the store.
Once inside, you're less likely to leave empty-handed. You'll pick up something similar, but pricier, to avoid a wasted trip.
The store wins: they sold you something, just not the deal. Next time you see that amazing price, you'll know the real game.
